clue.text: Felt, maybe, by the financially

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Felt, maybe, by the financially (7)' is cut short: the words after 'financially' are missing, so the pun on the bank sense cannot be shown

clue.text: Here it's right to take the ladies' side.

definitions.text: Here it's right to take the ladies' side.

parts.words: Here it's right to take the ladies' side
parts.note: reads like advice on picking sides, but describes the term for the female line of a family, named after the spinning staff

explanation.surface: A place where siding with the women is the correct thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The female branch of a family is traditionally called the spindle side, after the stick used in spinning, women's work.

clue.text: Cut to bits.

parts.words: Cut to bits
parts.note: reads as plain destruction, but points to the careful dissection of a body by a surgeon or student

explanation.definitionFit: To dissect a body part by part, or to analyse minutely, is exactly this verb's sense.

clue.text: Falstaff's long way round!

parts.words: Falstaff's long way round
parts.note: Shakespeare's fat knight Falstaff had a great waist measurement, so a long way round him

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's comic knight takes a lengthy detour.
explanation.definitionFit: Waist measurement or circumference; Falstaff's was famously huge.

clue.text: Effect a cross obstruction.

parts.words: Effect a cross obstruction
parts.note: cross looks like angry, but the word can mean crosswise; to block something is to obstruct it

explanation.surface: Put up an angry barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To frustrate or block, from an old word for crosswise, also the cross-bench in a rowing boat.

clue.text: Time's up for this drive anyhow.

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old order, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

parts.words: Time's up
parts.note: the letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: The deadline has come, so get moving any way you can.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum or driving force; a sense of urgency is a push forward.

clue.text: Unwelcome person-among the print rude remarks!

indicators.note: among says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.words: the print rude remarks

explanation.surface: Someone unwanted turns up among the printed insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forces their way in where they are not wanted.

clue.text: Manual offerings one might term them.

definitions.text: Manual offerings one might term them.

parts.words: Manual offerings one might term them
parts.note: manual looks like a handbook, but means of the hand: offers of one's hand in marriage

explanation.surface: Things handed over, as one might call them.
explanation.definitionFit: Offers of marriage, where one asks for or offers a hand.

clue.text: Singular form of very close attachment!

definitions.text: Singular form of very close attachment!

parts.words: Singular form of very close attachment
parts.note: singular hints at the one-word form of a close-fitting garment usually plural, and very close describes a firm hold

explanation.surface: A remarkable kind of devoted bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly fixed or close-fitting; also the singular of the leg garment.

clue.text: Do some successful cramming.

parts.words: Do some successful cramming
parts.note: cramming suggests exam revision, but here means stuffing oneself with food till full

explanation.surface: A student revises with good results.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill up completely, to gorge until no more can be taken.

clue.text: Warps — or gives one the bird? Could

indicators.note: could signals that the letters might be put into a different order

parts.words: Warps
parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: or
parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something twists, or someone is being jeered off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held ends on 'Could', probably displaced in the printing; it signals that WARPS and OR may be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A small common brown songbird, a familiar example of a bird.

clue.text: "Thrones built beyond mortal the Unapparent "(Shelley).

parts.words: Thrones built beyond mortal the Unapparent
parts.note: a line of Shelley's Adonais with one word left out, to be supplied after mortal

explanation.surface: A line from Shelley's elegy for Keats with a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonais reads 'thrones, built beyond mortal thought, Far in the Unapparent': the missing word is mental reflection.

clue.text: Quite a different thing from one chap!

definitions.text: Quite a different thing from one chap!

parts.words: Quite a different thing from one chap
parts.note: chap looks like a man, but cha is tea; a different thing from one serving is a second serving, and the phrase means something else entirely

explanation.surface: Something very unlike a particular fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a quite different matter, literally a second serving of the brew.

clue.text: Not the sort of look to warm one

definitions.text: Not the sort of look to warm one

parts.words: Not the sort of look to warm one
parts.note: an icy glance gives no warmth, describing a cold manner

explanation.surface: An unfriendly stare.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy, cold in manner; a cold stare chills.

clue.text: Nice trait, but somehow puzzling.

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

parts.words: Nice trait
parts.note: the letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A pleasant quality that is somehow baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Complicated and hard to work out, so baffling.

clue.text: Who, for instance, might be one's uncle!

definitions.text: Who, for instance, might be one's uncle!

parts.words: Who, for instance, might be one's uncle
parts.note: who is an example of a grammatical pronoun introducing a clause, and an uncle is a family member

explanation.surface: Asking who your uncle might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a family member such as an uncle and the grammatical class of pronoun to which who belongs.

clue.text: Given a proper start!

parts.words: Given a proper start
parts.note: a proper start means a formal admission into a society, with rites

explanation.definitionFit: Formally admitted to a group, or begun; started off properly.

clue.text: Still chivalrous, despite the dark inside?

definitions.text: Still chivalrous, despite the dark inside?

parts.words: Still chivalrous, despite the dark inside
parts.note: dark inside points to the word for darkness sitting inside the word for chivalrous, which stays noble all the same

explanation.surface: A gallant person stays courteous though gloomy within.
explanation.definitionFit: Befitting a chivalrous mounted warrior; the word contains the night.

clue.text: Like that moment we can't hold onto.

definitions.text: Like that moment we can't hold onto.

parts.words: Like that moment we can't hold onto
parts.note: describes a moment that slips away too quickly to keep

explanation.definitionFit: Passing swiftly, transient, so it cannot be held.

clue.text: Sounds an unfair way of shooting birds.

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard like another word

parts.words: an unfair way
parts.note: fouling is breaking the rules, playing in an unfair way

explanation.surface: Shooting game birds in a way that seems unsporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting wildfowl, shooting or trapping birds.

clue.text: Observation, possibly a bit distant.

parts.words: Observation, possibly a bit distant
parts.note: describes watching, perhaps from afar, as a spy would

explanation.definitionFit: Old word for spying or watching, the act of catching sight from a distance.

clue.text: "Unshaken unseduced unterrified. His he kept." (Milton.)

parts.words: Unshaken unseduced unterrified. His he kept
parts.note: Milton's Paradise Lost on Abdiel, with a word missing after His

explanation.definitionFit: Milton wrote 'Unshaken, unseduced, unterrified, His loyalty he kept': faithfulness is the missing word.

clue.text: An opening that may involve some sacrifice.

definitions.text: An opening that may involve some sacrifice.

parts.words: An opening that may involve some sacrifice
parts.note: opening looks like a job vacancy, but is a chess opening where a pawn is given up

explanation.surface: A job vacancy that demands self-denial.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess opening in which a pawn or piece is offered for advantage.

clue.text: The opposite, one would think, of rich.

definitions.text: The opposite, one would think, of rich.

parts.words: The opposite, one would think, of rich
parts.note: the rich are thought of as a leisured minority; the reverse of that is a labouring larger number

explanation.surface: What is contrary to wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: Leisured minority versus labouring majority: the phrase means a parliamentary margin big enough to govern.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary margin large enough to govern, literally a labouring larger number.

clue.text: In revolt — on the surface.

definitions.meaning: having come up to the top, as from water

explanation.surface: Rebelling, out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Having rebelled, or having come up to the top.

clue.text: A bit green this girl.

definitions.meaning: a shade of dull yellowish green

explanation.surface: This young woman is a little inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish-green colour and also a woman's first name.

clue.text: Just a moment!

parts.words: Just a moment
parts.note: an everyday plea for a brief wait, read literally as a point in time

explanation.definitionFit: A very brief point of time.

clue.text: Trim West Country fashion.

parts.words: Trim West Country fashion
parts.note: shipshape and the port's fashion is a saying for neat; the West Country is south-west England, home of this port

explanation.surface: A neat style of dress from south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The English port in the phrase shipshape and its fashion, meaning tidy.

clue.text: This should teach one how to deal big shots.

definitions.text: This should teach one how to deal big shots.

parts.words: This should teach one how to deal big shots
parts.note: big shots look like important people, but are shells from heavy artillery

explanation.surface: A course in handling important people.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of firing artillery, delivering large shells.

clue.text: A child full of grace, mine.

definitions.text: A child full of grace, mine.

parts.words: A child full of grace, mine
parts.note: the nursery rhyme Monday's Child says the child born on one particular weekday is full of grace

explanation.surface: Proud parent describing a graceful child.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme, the day of birth whose child is full of grace.
